html:
End of lease cleaning in Greer gets squeezed into the worst possible slot: after the truck is loaded and before the keys are due. A timeline fixes that. Below is a week-long plan, written for people who are moving into Greer, out of it, or across town, with the cleaning steps placed where they actually fit.

Greer straddles Greenville and Spartanburg counties (ZIPs 29650, 29651 and 29652), and the mix of housing is wide, from older homes near Downtown Greer and Trade Street to newer neighborhoods near GSP Airport and the BMW plant. A different house means a different plan, but the order of the week stays the same.

Seven days out: tidy as you pack

The cheapest cleaning you can do is the cleaning you do while packing. Empty one room at a time, and as each closet or cabinet goes bare, wipe it right then. Shelves are far easier to clean empty and before dust settles back on them. This is also the time to take down curtains and wipe the window sills while the room is still open.

Use this week to decide who does what. Are you cleaning on your own, or booking a team? If it is a team, the next step is the visit.

One more habit helps. Keep a small bag of the things you will need on the last day: a vacuum or broom, a few cloths, trash bags and a roll of paper towels. When the movers load the truck, those supplies are the first things buried. Set them by the front door and they stay reachable.

How much does end of lease cleaning cost in Greer?

We do not give a number over the phone or from a photo, and this is why: the price follows the home, not the date. The size (rooms and square feet) matters, and so does the condition the last occupant left it in. Appliances count too. The inside of the oven and refrigerator are included, but heavy grease takes more time. An empty home cleans faster than a furnished one, and a tight closing or key-return window may need more people on site.

The numbers differ for a one-bedroom and a family home with a finished basement, which is why we want to walk through it before quoting. If you are a seller, the buyer-facing side of that is covered in our post on cleaning a home before listing it in Greer. For a renter, the estimate is usually the quicker route to a firm number.

Moving day and the day after: the empty-house window

The best moment for the real cleaning is the gap between the last box leaving and the key handoff. The house is empty, every cabinet is reachable, and the floors are clear. Here is what a team does in that window.

  1. Dust ceilings, fans, vents and light fixtures.
  2. Clean inside and outside every kitchen cabinet and drawer, then the appliances inside and out.
  3. Scrub the bathrooms: toilet base, grout, glass and the insides of vanities.
  4. Do the closets, then baseboards, doors, frames and light switches.
  5. Wipe window sills, tracks and blinds.
  6. Vacuum and mop edge to edge, finishing at the front door.

Done in that order, nothing needs to be cleaned twice. If the house needs more than a standard turnover, we may suggest deep cleaning as a first step.

Our move-in and move-out cleaning covers both ends of the move with the same checklist, so you can treat the two homes as a pair. Many families book one visit for the old place and a second for the new one, a day apart.

Cleaning before you unpack at the new place

People forget half of the timeline: the home you are moving into. Even a house that looks fine has dust inside cabinets, a film on the shelves, and floors that have seen a lot of foot traffic from showings and movers. Moving-in cleaning is easiest while it is empty, so schedule it before the furniture arrives or in the first hours after the truck is parked. Shelves, drawers and closet floors are all within reach. Once boxes are stacked on the counters, you will never get that chance again.

Families with kids or pets often have a stronger reason to do this: you know exactly what is on those floors and what will go in those drawers. If you prefer products without a strong scent, ask about green cleaning during the estimate. For another example of this work, see move-in and move-out cleaning in Duncan.

It also helps to take a few photos of the home when you leave it, for your own records. If something is still on your plate the night before, the first thing to cut is the garage, not the kitchen. Greer renters and sellers who keep the focus on the kitchen, bathrooms and floors usually get the best return from their time. faqs: How far ahead should I book end of lease cleaning in Greer?
As soon as you have a move date. The days around the end of a month are the busiest, and the free in-home estimate needs to happen before the cleaning.
Should I clean before or after the movers leave?
Wipe shelves and cabinets as you pack, but do the main cleaning after the home is empty. Floors should always be last.
